                                        &= \dfrac {70} {100} \times 50 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {70 \times 50} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {35 \times 2 \times 50} {50 \times 2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {35 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {50}} {\cancel {50} \times \cancel 2} \\\\
                                        &= 35 \\\\
\text{People in Sita's results who can} &= 60 \% \ \text{of} \ 100 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {60} {100} \times 100 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {60 \times 100} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {60 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel {100}} \\\\
                                        &= 60 \\\\
\text{People in Tina's results who can} &= 50 \% \ \text{of} \ 200 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50} {100} \times 200 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \times 200} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \times 2 \times 100} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \times 2 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel {100}} \\\\
                                        &= 50 \times 2 \\\\
                                        &= 100
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
|          | Number of people who were tested     | Number of people who **can** taste the difference     | Number of people who **cannot** taste the difference     |
|:----:    |:--------------------------------:    |:-------------------------------------------------:    |:----------------------------------------------------:    |
| Ravi     |               $50$                   |          $35 \ \footnotesize{(1)}$                    |          $50 - 35 = 15 \ \footnotesize{(4)}$             |
| Sita     |               $100$                  |          $60 \ \footnotesize{(2)}$                    |         $100 - 60 = 40 \ \footnotesize{(5)}$             |
| Tina     |               $200$                  |         $100 \ \footnotesize{(3)}$                    |        $200 - 100 = 100 \ \footnotesize{(6)}$            |
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There are four unknown positive whole numbers.

The mean of the two smallest numbers is $3$.

The mean of the three smallest numbers is $5$.

The mean of all four numbers is $7$.

All the numbers are different and odd. 

What are the four numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There are four unknown positive whole numbers.
<emptyline>
The mean of the two smallest numbers is $3$.
<emptyline>
The mean of the three smallest numbers is $5$.
<emptyline>
The mean of all four numbers is $7$.
<emptyline>
All the numbers are different and odd. 
<emptyline>
What are the four numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the four unknown numbers $= a, b, c, d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a + b} {2}                          &= 3 \\\\
a + b                                       &= 3 \times 2 \\\\
a + b                                       &= 6  & (1)\\\\
\dfrac {a + b + c} {3}                      &= 3 \\\\
a + b + c                                   &= 5 \times 3 \\\\
a + b + c                                   &= 15  & (2) \\\\
\dfrac {a + b + c + d} {4}                  &= 3 \\\\
a + b + c + d                               &= 7 \times 4 \\\\
a + b + c + d                               &= 28  & (3)
\end{aligned}
$

Let's subtract equation $(2)$ from $(3)$ to get the value of $d$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b + c + d - (a + b + c)       &= 28 - 15 \\\\
a + b + c + d - a - b - c         &= 13 \\\\
d                                 &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

Let's subtract equation $(1)$ from $(2)$ to get the value of $c$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b + c - (a + b)       &= 15 - 6 \\\\
a + b + c - a - b         &= 9 \\\\
c                         &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Let's infer the value of $a$ and $b$ which meets the critiera below using trial and error method.

- Both the numbers are odd.
- They are not equal.

<br />

|   $a$ |     $b$     |   Different  |
|:-----:|:-----------:|:------------:|
|  $1$  | $6 - 1 = 5$ |     Yes      |
|  $3$  | $6 - 3 = 3$ |     No       |

$a = 1$

$b = 5$

Numbers $= 1, 5, 9, 13$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1, 5, 9, 13$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three bicycles are priced at $\pounds 79, \pounds 80$ and $\pounds 84$. If the shopkeeper decided to sell them for the same total amount, but made the three prices equal, what would each cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three bicycles are priced at $\pounds 79, \pounds 80$ and $\pounds 84$. If the shopkeeper decided to sell them for the same total amount, but made the three prices equal, what would each cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Cost of each bicycle}          &= \text{Average of three bicycles} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {\text{Total cost}} {\text{Number of bicycles}} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {79 + 80 + 84 } {3} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {243} {3} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {81 \times 3} {3} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {81 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} \\\\
                                      &= \pounds 81
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 81$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The following table shows the golf scores that John obtained in $5$ matches with two unknown scores $X$ and $Y$. 

{/*
Score, 65, X, 70, 74, Y
*/}

| Score     | $65$     | $X$     | $70$     | $74$     | $Y$     |
|-------    |----      |---      |----      |----      |---      |

If the modal score is $70$ and the mean score is $72$ find $X$ and $Y$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The following table shows the golf scores that John obtained in $5$ matches with two unknown scores $X$ and $Y$. 
<emptyline>
{/*
Score, 65, X, 70, 74, Y
*/}
<emptyline>
| Score     | $65$     | $X$     | $70$     | $74$     | $Y$     |
|-------    |----      |---      |----      |----      |---      |
<emptyline>
If the modal score is $70$ and the mean score is $72$ find $X$ and $Y$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The mode is $70$ for the list of five numbers, and there is only one $70$ in the known numbers, so at least one of the unknown numbers will be $70$ too.

$X = 70$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {65 + X + 70 + 74 + Y} {5}       &= 72 \\\\
\dfrac {65 + 70 + 70 + 74 + Y} {5}      &= 72 \\\\
\dfrac {Y + 279} {5}                    &= 72 \\\\
Y + 279                                 &= 72 \times 5 \\\\
Y + 279                                 &= 360 \\\\
Y                                       &= 360 - 279 \\\\
Y                                       &= 81
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$X$ $=$ $70$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$Y$ $=$ $81$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean age of the five members of the `Macaroon $5$' boy band is $18$. 

A new member joins the band. His age is $24$. 
What is the new mean age of the group?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The mean age of the five members of the `Macaroon $5$' boy band is $18$. 
<emptyline>
A new member joins the band. His age is $24$. 
What is the new mean age of the group?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total previous ages}      &= 18 \times 5 \\\\
                                &= 90 \\\\
\text{New mean}                 &= \dfrac {90 + 24} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {114} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {6 \times 19} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 19} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                                &= 19
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Find $4$ numbers which have a mean of $7$, a median of $8$ and a mode of $9$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find $4$ numbers which have a mean of $7$, a median of $8$ and a mode of $9$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

If mode is $9$, then at least $2$ numbers must be $9$.

There are even count of numbers, the median will be the mean of the middle two values. As the median is $8$, $9$ are not the middle values.

Let the four numbers in ascending order $= a, b, 9, 9$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a + b + 9 + 9} {4}              &= 7 \\\\
a + b + 9 + 9                           &= 7 \times 4 \\\\
a + b + 18                              &= 28 \\\\
a + b                                   &= 28 - 18 \\\\
a + b                                   &= 10   & (1)
\end{aligned}
$

Lets arrange the numbers in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Ordered numbers}          &= a, \quad \maroonC{b}, \quad \maroonC{9}, \quad 9 \\\\
\dfrac {b + 9} {2}              &= 8 \\\\
b + 9                           &= 8 \times 2 \\\\
b + 9                           &= 16 \\\\
b                               &= 16 - 9 \\\\
b                               &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Lets use value of $b$ in equation $(1)$ to get the value of $a$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b                   &= 10 \\\\
a                       &= 10 - b \\\\
a                       &= 10 - 7 \\\\
a                       &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

Required four numbers $= 3, 7, 9, 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3, 7, 9, 9$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean weight of $5$ children is $45 \ \text{kg}$.

The mean weight of the lightest three children is $42 \ \text{kg}$ and the mean weight of the heaviest three children is $49 \ \text{kg}$. 

What is the median weight of the children in $\text{kg}?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The mean weight of $5$ children is $45 \ \text{kg}$.
<emptyline>
The mean weight of the lightest three children is $42 \ \text{kg}$ and the mean weight of the heaviest three children is $49 \ \text{kg}$. 
<emptyline>
What is the median weight of the children in $\text{kg}?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the weights of $5$ children $= a, b, c, d, e$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a + b + c + d + e} {5}        &= 45 \\\\
a + b + c + d + e                     &= 45 \times 5 \\\\
a + b + c + d + e                     &= 225   & (1) \\\\
\dfrac {a + b + c} {3}                &= 42 \\\\
a + b + c                             &= 42 \times 3 \\\\
a + b + c                             &= 126   & (2) \\\\
\dfrac {b + c + d} {3}                &= 49 \\\\
c + d + e                             &= 49 \times 3 \\\\
c + d + e                             &= 147   & (3)
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substract equation $(1)$ from the sum of equation $(2)$ and equation $(3)$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b + c + c + d + e - (a + b + c + d + e)             &= 126 + 147 - 225 \\\\
a + b + 2c + d + e - a - b - c - d - e                  &= 273 - 225 \\\\
a - a + b - b + 2c - c + d - d + e - e                  &= 48 \\\\
c                                                       &= 48 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned}
$

Median weight of the children $= 48 \ \text{kg}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$48 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$25$ students have taken an exam and the mean number of marks is recorded as $83$. 

The examiner subsequently awards $5$ additional marks to $9$ of the students and takes away $2$ marks from $10$ other students. 

What will the new mean mark be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$25$ students have taken an exam and the mean number of marks is recorded as $83$. 
<emptyline>
The examiner subsequently awards $5$ additional marks to $9$ of the students and takes away $2$ marks from $10$ other students. 
<emptyline>
What will the new mean mark be?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total marks earlier}              &= 25 \times 83 \\\\
                                        &= 2075 \\\\
\text{Total marks later}                &= 2075 + 9 \times 5 - 10 \times 2 \\\\
                                        &= 2075 + 45 - 20 \\\\
                                        &= 2100 \\\\
\text{New Mean}                         &= \dfrac {2100} {25} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {25 \times 84} {25} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {25} \times 84} {\cancel {25}} \\\\
                                        &= 84
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$84$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Calculate the average (mean) of the numbers below:

$94 \quad 30 \quad 8\quad 33\quad 97\quad 10$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Calculate the average (mean) of the numbers below:
<emptyline>
$94 \quad 30 \quad 8\quad 33\quad 97\quad 10$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean}     &= \dfrac {94 + 30 + 8 + 33 + 97 + 10} {6} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {272} {6} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {6 \times 37} {6} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 37} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                &= 37
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$37$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean (average) of a set of six numbers is $10$. The number $25$ is removed from the set.

Calculate the mean of the remaining numbers. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The mean (average) of a set of six numbers is $10$. The number $25$ is removed from the set.
<emptyline>
Calculate the mean of the remaining numbers. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sum of 6 numbers}               &= 10 \times 6 \\\\
                                      &= 60 \\\\
\text{Mean of the remaining numbers}  &= \dfrac{60 - 25}{5} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac{35}{5} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac{7 \times 5}{5} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
                                      &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A set of five different positive integers has a mean (average) of $20$ and a median of $18$.

What is the greatest possible integer in the set? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A set of five different positive integers has a mean (average) of $20$ and a median of $18$.
<emptyline>
What is the greatest possible integer in the set? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$

- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the five different positive numbers $= a1, a2, a3, a4, a5$

Let's arrange the numbers in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Ordered numbers}   &= a1, \quad a2, \quad \maroonC{a3}, \quad a4, \quad a5 \\\\
\text{Median}            &= a3 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a3                                              &= 18 \\\\
\dfrac {a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5} {5}             &= 20 \\\\
a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5                          &= 20 \times 5 \\\\
a1 + a2 + 18 + a4 + a5                          &= 100 \\\\
a1 + a2 + a4 + a5                               &= 100 - 18 \\\\
a1 + a2 + a4 + a5                               &= 82
\end{aligned}
$

Minimum positive value of $a1 = 1$

Minimum positive value of $a2 = 2$

Minimum positive value of $a4 = 19$

Using minimum possible values of $a1, a2$ and $a4$ to find the maximum possible value of $a5$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a1 + a2 + a4 + a5               &= 82 \\\\
1 + 2 + 19 + a5                 &= 82 \\\\
22 + a5                         &= 82 \\\\
a5                              &= 82 - 22 \\\\
a5                              &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Greatest possible value in the set $= 60$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$60$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean (average) of a set of six numbers is $10$. The number $17$ is added to the set of numbers.

Calculate the mean of the new set. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The mean (average) of a set of six numbers is $10$. The number $17$ is added to the set of numbers.
<emptyline>
Calculate the mean of the new set. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sum of numbers}   &= 10 \times 6 \\\\
                        &= 60 \\\\
\text{New mean}         &= \dfrac {60 + 17} {7} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {77} {7} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {7 \times 11} {7} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {\cancel 7 \times 11} {\cancel 7} \\\\
                        &= 11
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$11$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Determine the mean, median and mode of the following set of numbers: 

$16, \quad 9, \quad 11, \quad 13, \quad 11, \quad 15$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Determine the mean, median and mode of the following set of numbers: 
<emptyline>
$16, \quad 9, \quad 11, \quad 13, \quad 11, \quad 15$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean}     &= \dfrac {16 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 11 + 15} {6} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {75} {6} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {3 \times 25} {3 \times 2} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 25} {\cancel 3 \times 2} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {25} {2} \\\\
                &= 12.5
\end{aligned}
$

Let's arrange the numbers in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Numbers}           &= 16, \quad 9, \quad 11, \quad 13, \quad 11, \quad 15 \\\\
\text{Ordered numbers}   &= 9, \quad 11, \quad \maroonC{11}, \quad \maroonC{13}, \quad 15, \quad 16 \\\\
\text{Median}            &= \dfrac {11 + 13} {2} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {24} {2} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {2 \times 12} {2} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 12} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                         &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Lets look for the value that occurs the most.

|   Number  |   Count   |
|:---------:|:---------:|
|   $9$     |    $1$    |
|   $11$    |    $2$    |
|   $13$    |    $1$    |
|   $15$    |    $1$    |
|   $16$    |    $1$    |

Mode $= 11$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mean $=$ $12.5$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Median $=$ $12$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mode $=$ $11$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean of four numbers $x, 4, 5$ and $y$  is $5$ and the range of the numbers is $7$.  Find $x$ and  $y$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The mean of four numbers $x, 4, 5$ and $y$  is $5$ and the range of the numbers is $7$.  Find $x$ and  $y$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{x + 4 + 5 + y}{4}        &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{9 + x + y}{4}            &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{9 + x + y}{4}            &= 5 \\\\
9 + x + y                       &= 5 \times 4 \\\\
9 + x + y                       &= 20 \\\\
x + y                           &= 20 -  9 \\\\
x + y                           &= 11
\end{aligned}
$

Lets find out the value of $x$ and $y$ which satisfies the condition:

- The range is $7$
- $x + y = 11$

| x |       y      |         Range      |
|:-:|:------------:|:------------------:|
|$1$|  $11-1 = 10$ |       10 - 1 = 9   |
|$2$|  $11-2 = 9$  |       9 - 2 = 7    |
|$3$|  $11-3 = 8$  |       8 - 3 = 5    |
|$4$|  $11-4 = 7$  |       7 - 4 = 3    |
|$5$|  $11-5 = 6$  |       6 - 4 = 2    |
|$6$|  $11-6 = 5$  |       6 - 4 = 2    |

A quick check shows that $2$ and $9$ meets the criteria above.

$x = 2$

$y = 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2$ and $9$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Eight apples are placed in a bag. The mean weight of the eight apples is $50 \ \text{g}$.  When an extra apple is added the mean weight increases to $52 \ \text{g}$. 

What is the weight of the extra apple?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Eight apples are placed in a bag. The mean weight of the eight apples is $50 \ \text{g}$.  When an extra apple is added the mean weight increases to $52 \ \text{g}$. 
<emptyline>
What is the weight of the extra apple?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the weight of the extra apple $= w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {8 \times 50 + w} {9}    &= 52 \\\\
400 + w                         &= 52 \times 9 \\\\
400 + w                         &= 468 \\\\
w                               &= 468 - 400 \\\\
w                               &= 68 \ \text{g}
\end{aligned}
$

Weight of extra apple $= 68 \ \text{g}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$68 \ \text{g}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$A$, $B$ and $C$ are numbers.

The mean of $A$ and $B$ is $40$

The mean of $B$ and $C$ is $35$

All three numbers add up to $100$

What are $A$, $B$ and $C \text{?}$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$A$, $B$ and $C$ are numbers.
<emptyline>
The mean of $A$ and $B$ is $40$
<emptyline>
The mean of $B$ and $C$ is $35$
<emptyline>
All three numbers add up to $100$
<emptyline>
What are $A$, $B$ and $C \text{?}$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {A + B} {2}      &= 40 \\\\
A + B                   &= 40 \times 2 \\\\
A + B                   &= 80  & (1)  \\\\
\dfrac {B + C} {2}      &= 35 \\\\
B + C                   &= 35 \times 2 \\\\
B + C                   &= 70  & (2) \\\\
A + B + C               &= 100 & (3)
\end{aligned}
$

Let's subtract equation $(1)$ from equation $(3)$ to get the value of $C$.

$
\begin{aligned}
A + B + C - (A + B)             &= 100 - 80 \\\\
A - A + B - B + C               &= 20 \\\\
C                               &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

Let's use the value of $C$ in equation $(2)$ to get the value of $B$.

$
\begin{aligned}
B + C           &= 70 \\\\
B + 20          &= 70 \\\\
B               &= 70 - 20 \\\\
B               &= 50
\end{aligned}
$

Let's use the value of $B$ in equation $(1)$ to get the value of $A$.

$
\begin{aligned}
A + B           &= 80 \\\\
A + 50          &= 80 \\\\
A               &= 80 - 50 \\\\
A               &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$A$ $=$ $30$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$B$ $=$ $50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$C$ $=$ $20$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I am thinking of three different, positive, whole numbers.

The mean of my three numbers is $8$.

The median of my three numbers is $9$.

Write down one possible set of three numbers that my numbers could be. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I am thinking of three different, positive, whole numbers.
<emptyline>
The mean of my three numbers is $8$.
<emptyline>
The median of my three numbers is $9$.
<emptyline>
Write down one possible set of three numbers that my numbers could be. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

One possible set of numbers $= 5, 9, 10$

Let's verify.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean}     &= \dfrac {5 + 9 + 10} {3} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {3 \times 8} {3} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 8} {\cancel 3} \\\\
                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Let's arrange the numbers in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Ordered numbers}      &= 5, \quad \maroonC{9}, \quad 10 \\\\
\text{Median}               &= 9
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5, 9, 10$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The number of goals scored by St Francis' netball team in their last $10$ games are as follows.

$7 \quad 2 \quad 12 \quad 10 \quad 5 \quad 3 \quad  7 \quad  11 \quad  6\quad  4$

Find the mean 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The number of goals scored by St Francis' netball team in their last $10$ games are as follows.
<emptyline>
$7 \quad 2 \quad 12 \quad 10 \quad 5 \quad 3 \quad  7 \quad  11 \quad  6\quad  4$
<emptyline>
Find the mean 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Mean} &= \dfrac {7 + 2 + 12 + 10 + 5 + 3 + 7 + 11 + 6 + 4} {10} \\\\
             &= \dfrac {67} {10}  \\\\
             &= 6.7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6.7$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Snow White wanted to know the mean height of the Seven Dwarves. One day she measured them all as they left for work and calculated their mean height as $114.5 \ \text{cm}$. Grumpy complained that she had missed him out and had measured Dopey twice without him noticing. If Grumpy is $14 \ \text{cm}$ taller than Dopey, what is the mean height of the Seven Dwarves?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Snow White wanted to know the mean height of the Seven Dwarves. One day she measured them all as they left for work and calculated their mean height as $114.5 \ \text{cm}$. Grumpy complained that she had missed him out and had measured Dopey twice without him noticing. If Grumpy is $14 \ \text{cm}$ taller than Dopey, what is the mean height of the Seven Dwarves?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total miscalculated height}\      &= 114.5 \times 7 \\\\
                                        &= 801.5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Actual total height}\             &= 801.5 + 14  \\\\
                                        &= 815.5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Mean height}                      &= \dfrac {815.5} {7} \\\\
                                        &= 116.5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$ 
</div>
</div>

Let the third number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {5 + 5 + a} {3}  &= 6 \\\\
10 + a                  &= 3 \times 6 \\\\
10 + a                  &= 18 \\\\
a                       &= 18 - 10 \\\\
a                       &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 5, 5, 8$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Five bags of rice have masses of $75 \ \text{g}, 64 \ \text{g}, 53 \ \text{g}, 62 \ \text{g}$ and $46 \ \text{g}$.
Find the mean mass of a bag of rice. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Five bags of rice have masses of $75 \ \text{g}, 64 \ \text{g}, 53 \ \text{g}, 62 \ \text{g}$ and $46 \ \text{g}$.
Find the mean mass of a bag of rice. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean mass}    &= \dfrac {75 + 64 + 53 + 62 + 46} {5} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {300} {5} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {5 \times 60} {5} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 60} {\cancel 5} \\\\
                    &= 60 \ \text{g}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$60 \ \text{g}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The mean of Jane's six Mathematics test is $89 \%$. After her 
seventh test the mean increased to $90 \%$. 
What did Jane score in her seventh test?

- $95 \%$
- $89 \%$
- $96 \%$
- $90 \%$
- $93 \%$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

seventh test the mean increased to $90 \%$. 
What did Jane score in her seventh test?
<emptyline>
- $95 \%$
- $89 \%$
- $96 \%$
- $90 \%$
- $93 \%$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Jane's score in her seventh test $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {6 \times 89 + a} {7}    &= 90 \\\\
\dfrac {534 + a} {7}            &= 90 \\\\
534 + a                         &= 90 \times 7 \\\\
534 + a                         &= 630 \\\\
a                               &= 630 - 534 \\\\
a                               &= 96
\end{aligned}
$

Seventh test score $= 96 \ \%$
</div>
</div>

**Answer**

$96 \ \%$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In this innings the opening pair of batsmen scored an average of $39.5$ runs. What was the average score of the remaining nine members of the team?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In this innings the opening pair of batsmen scored an average of $39.5$ runs. What was the average score of the remaining nine members of the team?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total runs by openers}            &= 39.5 \times 2 \\\\
                                        &= 79 \\\\
\text{Total runs by rest 9 players}     &= 187 - 79 \\\\
                                        &= 108 \\\\
\text{Average runs of 9 players}        &= \dfrac {108} {9} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {9 \times 12} {9} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel 9 \times 12} {\cancel 9} \\\\
                                        &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Rishi pays an additional $\pounds 31$ for a special pass which gives front of line access to all rides throughout the day. 
He experiences $14$ rides. Does the special pass provide value for money? Give reasons for your answer.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Rishi pays an additional $\pounds 31$ for a special pass which gives front of line access to all rides throughout the day. 
He experiences $14$ rides. Does the special pass provide value for money? Give reasons for your answer.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average cost per ride}    &= \dfrac {37.6 + 31} {14} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {68.6} {14} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {686} {14 \times 10} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {14 \times 49} {14 \times 10} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {14} \times 49} {\cancel {14} \times 10} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {49} {10} \\\\
                                &= \pounds 4.90
\end{aligned}
$

The average cost per ride is more with special pass, so it does not provide the value for money.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

No

</div>
</div>

Active Eight had $4$ runners in their team.

Find the mean time for each runner in this team by dividing their total time by $4$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

</code></pre>

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean time}    &= \dfrac {51.2} {4} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {512} {4 \times 10} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 128} {4 \times 10} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 128} {\cancel 4 \times 10} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {128} {10} \\\\
                    &= 12.8 \ \text{s}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

\begin{aligned}
\text{Total number of people}   &= (4 \times 3) + (5 \times 4 + 2) + (2 \times 4 + 3) + (1 \times 4 + 2) + 9 \\\\
                                &= 12 + 20 + 2 + 8 + 3 + 4 + 2 + 9 \\\\
                                &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Two numbers have a mean of $12$ and a range of $6$. 

What are the two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two numbers have a mean of $12$ and a range of $6$. 
<emptyline>
What are the two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$

- ABBR: $\text{Range} = \text{Highest number} - \text{Lowest number}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a + b} {2}      &= 12 \\\\
a + b                   &= 12 \times 2 \\\\
a + b                   &= 24 & (1) \\\\
b - a                   &= 6  & (2)
\end{aligned}
$

Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. Add the two equations to eliminate $a$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b                   &= 24 \\\\
b - a                   &= 6  \\\\
a + b + b -a            &= 24 + 6 \\\\
2b                      &= 30 \\\\
b                       &= \dfrac {30} {2} \\\\
b                       &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the initial equations to find the value of $a$.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b                       &= 24  \\\\
a + 15                      &= 24 \\\\
a                           &= 24 - 15 \\\\
a                           &= 9
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9$

</div>

$15$

</div>

                              &= \dfrac {15} {2} \\\\
                              &= 7.5
\end{aligned}

- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\text{Ordered temperatures}   &= 3, \quad 9, \quad \maroonC{11}, \quad \maroonC{21}, \quad 24, \quad 29 \\\\
\text{Median temperature}     &= \dfrac {11 + 21} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {32} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {2 \times 16} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 16} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                              &= 16 \degree \text{C}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The cost of a bottle of lemonade in four different shops is

$42 \ \text{p}, 38 \ \text{p}, 40 \ \text{p}$ and $36 \ \text{p}$.

Calculate the mean price of a bottle of lemonade.

![papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2009/sample-paper-4/s01-q15-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2009/sample-paper-4/s01-q15-s01-i00.png "papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2009/sample-paper-4/s01-q15-s01-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The cost of a bottle of lemonade in four different shops is
<emptyline>
$42 \ \text{p}, 38 \ \text{p}, 40 \ \text{p}$ and $36 \ \text{p}$.
<emptyline>
Calculate the mean price of a bottle of lemonade.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean price}       &= \dfrac {40 + 42 + 38 + 36} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {156} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {39 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {39 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
                        &= 39 \ \text{p}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Calculate the mean of these numbers.

$9 \quad 14 \quad 7 \quad 17 \quad 8$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

             &= \dfrac {55} {5} \\\\
             &= \dfrac {11 \times 5} {5} \\\\
             &= \dfrac {11 \times \cancel{5}} {\cancel{5}} \\\\
             &= 11
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Mrs Fowler keeps chickens.

The table shows how many eggs her chickens laid on each weekday last week.

|Days      |Number of eggs|
|:--------:|:------------:|
|Monday    |$4$           |
|Tuesday   |$?$           |
|Wednesday |$4$           |
|Thursday  |$3$           |
|Friday    |$11$          |

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png")

The mean number of eggs laid from Monday to Friday last week was $6$.

How many eggs were laid on Tuesday?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mrs Fowler keeps chickens.
<emptyline>
The table shows how many eggs her chickens laid on each weekday last week.
<emptyline>
|Days      |Number of eggs|
|:--------:|:------------:|
|Monday    |$4$           |
|Tuesday   |$?$           |
|Wednesday |$4$           |
|Thursday  |$3$           |
|Friday    |$11$          |
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
The mean number of eggs laid from Monday to Friday last week was $6$.
<emptyline>
How many eggs were laid on Tuesday?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of eggs laid on Tuesday $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {4 + a + 4 + 3 + 11} {5}         &= 6 \\\\
\dfrac {a + 22} {5}                     &= 6 \\\\
a + 22                                  &= 6 \times 5 \\\\
a + 22                                  &= 30 \\\\
a                                       &= 30 - 22 \\\\
a                                       &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number of eggs laid on Tuesday $= a$

\dfrac {4 + a + 4 + 3 + 11} {5}         &= 6 \\\\

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the total length of the $3$ tracks?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the total length of the $3$ tracks?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total length}    &= 4 \ \text{min } 45 \ \text{sec} + 5 \ \text{min } 5  \ \text{sec} + 4 \ \text{min } 40 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                        &= 4 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 45 \ \text{sec} + 5 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 5 \ \text{sec} + 4 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 40 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                        &= 240 + 45 + 300 + 5 + 240 + 40 \\\\
                        &= 870 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                        &= 14 \ \text{min} \ 30 \ \text{sec}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

**Question**

Vanessa also practised on Saturday.

Her mean practice time for all $6 \ \text{days}$ was $15 \ \text{minutes}$.

Work out for how many minutes Vanessa practised on Saturday.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Vanessa also practised on Saturday.
<emptyline>
Her mean practice time for all $6 \ \text{days}$ was $15 \ \text{minutes}$.
<emptyline>
Work out for how many minutes Vanessa practised on Saturday.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let number of minutes Vanessa practiced on Saturday $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {10 + 14 + 6 + 10 + 15 + a} {6}          &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {55 + a} {6}                             &= 15 \\\\
55 + a                                          &= 15 \times 6 \\\\
55 + a                                          &= 90 \\\\
a                                               &= 90 - 55 \\\\
a                                               &= 35 \ \text{min}
\end{aligned}
$

Practise on Saturday $= 35 \ \text{min}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$35 \ \text{min}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Work out the total time that Yoshi takes to make the $4$ origami models.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Work out the total time that Yoshi takes to make the $4$ origami models.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total time taken}        &= 5 \ \text{min } 20 \ \text{sec} + 4 \ \text{min } 44 \ \text{sec} + 2 \ \text{min } 3 \ \text{sec} + 8 \ \text{min } 17 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                                &= 5 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 20 \ \text{sec} + 4 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 44 \ \text{sec} + 2 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 3 \ \text{sec} + 8 \times 60 \ \text{sec} + 17 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                                &= 300 + 20 + 240 + 44 + 120 + 3 + 480 + 17 \\\\
                                &= 1224 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                                &= 20 \ \text{min } 24 \ \text{sec}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                            &= 306 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                            &= 5 \ \text{min } 6 \ \text{sec}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Range} = \text{Highest number} - \text{Lowest number}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Range}   &= 8 \ \text{min } 17 \ \text{sec} - 2 \ \text{min } 3 \ \text{sec} \\\\

                &= 497 - 123 \\\\
                &= 374 \ \text{sec} \\\\
                &= 6 \ \text{min } 14 \ \text{sec}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Let's arrange the shoe sizes in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Shoe sizes}             &= 9, \quad 1 \dfrac {1} {2}, \quad 5, \quad 1 \dfrac {1} {2}, \quad 3, \quad 4 \\\\
\text{Ordered shoe sizes}     &= 1 \dfrac {1} {2}, \quad 1 \dfrac {1} {2}, \quad \maroonC{3}, \quad \maroonC{4}, \quad 5, \quad 9 \\\\
\text{Median shoe size}       &= \dfrac {3 + 4} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {7} {2} \\\\
                              &= 3 \dfrac {1} {2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Mean shoe size}   &= \dfrac {1 \dfrac {1} {2} + 1 \dfrac {1} {2} + 3 + 4 + 5 + 9} {6} \\\\

                        &= \dfrac {3 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 9} {6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {24} {6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {6 \times 4} {6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 4} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                        &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

**Question**

Jane has recorded the shoe size of every girl in her class.

Her results are shown in the table below.

|shoe size        |$3$|$4$ |$5$|$6$|
|:---------------:|:-:|:--:|:-:|:-:|
|number of people |$2$|$12$|$7$|$1$|

Jane says “The mode is $12$”.

Annabel says “The mode is $4$”.

Who is correct? Give a reason for your answer.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Joanne's marks in five spelling tests are: 

$7 \quad 9 \quad 8 \quad 7 \quad 6$

What is the range of her marks?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

                &= 3
\end{aligned}

**Answer**

$3$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Janet's marks on five mental arithmetic tests are:

$15 \quad 19 \quad 13 \quad 18 \quad 20$

What is her mean (average) mark?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Janet's marks on five mental arithmetic tests are:
<emptyline>
$15 \quad 19 \quad 13 \quad 18 \quad 20$
<emptyline>
What is her mean (average) mark?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average marks}            &= \dfrac {15 + 19 + 13 + 18 + 20} {5} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {85} {5} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {17 \times 5} {5} \\\\
                                &= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$17$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a list of numbers:

the **mode** is the number which occurs the most often;

the **median** is the number which is in the middle of the list when the numbers have been put in order;

the **mean** is the sum of all the numbers divided by how many numbers there are in the list.

For example, for the list $1, 4, 7, 1, 2$

mode $= 1$, median $= 2$, mean $= \dfrac{15}{5} = 3$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the mode, the median, and the mean for the list $8, 5, 2, 16, 6, 5, 7$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the mode, the median, and the mean for the list $8, 5, 2, 16, 6, 5, 7$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: If there is an odd number of numbers, the median is the middle number. If there is an even count of numbers, the median is the average of the middle two numbers.

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let's use a frequency table to find the mode.

| Number    | Count     |
|:------:   |:-----:    |
|   $2$     |    $1$    |
|   $5$     |    $2$    |
|   $6$     |    $1$    |
|   $7$     |    $1$    |
|   $8$     |    $1$    |
|   $16$    |    $1$    |

Mode $= 5$

Let's arrange the numbers in ascending order.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Numbers}           &= 8, \quad 5, \quad 2, \quad 16, \quad 6, \quad 5, \quad 7 \\\\
\text{Ordered numbers}   &= 2, \quad 5, \quad 5, \quad \maroonC{6}, \quad 7, \quad 8, \quad 16 \\\\
\text{Median}            &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Now let's calculate the median for the list.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Mean}    &= \dfrac {2 + 5 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 16} {7} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {49} {7} \\\\
                &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mode $=$ $5$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Median $=$ $6$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mean $=$ $7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Write down a list of three whole numbers for which the mode is $4$ and the mean is $6$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write down a list of three whole numbers for which the mode is $4$ and the mean is $6$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The mode is $4$ for the list of three numbers, so at least two numbers will be $4$.

Let the third number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a + 4 + 4} {3}                  &= 6 \\\\
\dfrac {a + 8} {3}                      &= 6 \\\\
a + 8                                   &= 6 \times 3 \\\\
a + 8                                   &= 18 \\\\
a                                       &= 18 - 8 \\\\
a                                       &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 4, 4, 10$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4, 4, 10$

</div>
</div>
